title: Converting a struct with a single get<T>()
summary: Put to_json and from_json in the same namespace as the type and ADL finds them, all the way up to vector<User>. When the fields pile up, hand them to the _WITH_DEFAULT macro.

turns.user: every time i turn a list of Users into json i write a for loop around user_to_json. cant i just do j.get<std::vector<User>>()

assistant.body: Sure. nlohmann/json looks for per-type conversions in free functions named to_json and from_json. Give it those two with the expected parameters and it builds get<User>() for you, along with User inside a vector or a map. Here is user_json.h with the two functions rewritten.
Here's users.cpp. The loops go away.

turns.user: doesnt compile. no matching member function for call to 'get' and then a wall of notes about get_impl

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous version left both functions in the global namespace. The library calls to_json unqualified from inside nlohmann, so the only functions it can find are the ones ADL reaches, which means those in namespace app, where the argument type app::User lives. The global ones were never candidates, so every get_impl overload dropped out. Wrapping both functions in namespace app fixes it.

sed -i '' -e 's/^#include "model\/user.h"$/&\
\
namespace app {/' -e '$a\
\
}  // namespace app' src/model/user_json.h

turns.user: builds now. but some old data has no tags and it throws out_of_range. also want a role field, viewer if missing. and am i writing these by hand forever every time a field gets added?

assistant.body: Short answer: no. List the type and its members in NLOHMANN_DEFINE_TYPE_NON_INTRUSIVE_WITH_DEFAULT and it generates the same to_json and from_json. The _WITH_DEFAULT flavour fills a missing key with that member of User{}, so the default lives in the member initializer. The macro just expands to functions, so it still goes inside namespace app.

sed -i '' 's/^  std::vector<std::string> tags;$/&\
  std::string role = "viewer";/' src/model/user.h

TL;DR: data without tags gets an empty vector, and data without role gets viewer. Caveat: name becomes optional too and quietly turns into an empty string. If name has to stay required, go back to the two handwritten functions and read just name with at().
